newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast prods mixed following NYMEX, Tosco.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast prods mixed following NYMEX, Tosco.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices were mixed Monday afternoon, traders said, following last week's rally caused by a Tosco refinery fire, which shut a key gasoline-making unit, traders said.
Traders said a bearish 1.01 million barrel build in West Coast gasoline stocks last week was offset by the shutdown of the northern California refinery, brokers said.
Offers for CARB grade gasoline in San Francisco were talked unchanged from late Friday levels of 79 cents a gallon, while conventional bids also steadied at 75 cents.
Los Angeles CARB for all February deliveries was seen notionally unchanged at 81 cents.

Meanwhile, distillates were directionless, with jet fuel in the Bay off one cent to 79/80 cents a gallon in line with falling U.S. Gulf prices and upcoming imports. Los Angeles material was a penny higher than the Bay after fallig a cent.
But San Francisco low sulphur diesel firmed 1.50 cents, still reeling from the effects of the Tosco fire and a slight uptick in NYMEX heating oil futures, which rose 0.52 cents to 67.29 cents.
CARB diesel in northern California was notionally much higher at 79.50/80 cents, versus 76/77 cents seen Friday.
